interactions.label: A man taking sildenafil can safely take sublingual glyceryl trinitrate for chest

params.question: A man taking sildenafil can safely take sublingual glyceryl trinitrate for chest pain, as long as he waits a few hours after his sildenafil dose.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Not quite — this combination is dangerous regardless of spacing. Sildenafil and glyceryl trinitrate both act on the nitric oxide–cGMP pathway, and together they cause cGMP to build up far beyond what either drug alone would cause, producing severe hypotension. That is why it is an absolute contraindication with no safe interval.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is an absolute contraindication, not a timing issue. Both drugs converge on the same nitric oxide–cGMP pathway: nitrates raise cGMP and sildenafil blocks its breakdown, so together they cause a severe, sometimes fatal, drop in blood pressure. Nitrates must be avoided for the drug's full duration of action (about 24 hours for sildenafil/vardenafil, 48 hours for tadalafil), not just a few hours.

interactions.label: A young man is prescribed finasteride for male pattern hair loss. Which of the f

params.question: A young man is prescribed finasteride for male pattern hair loss. Which of the following best explains why finasteride reduces hair loss and shrinks the prostate without significantly affecting his libido or muscle mass?

answers.text: Finasteride directly blocks the androgen receptor in all androgen-sensitive tissues

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Finasteride is not an androgen receptor antagonist — it does not block the receptor itself. It acts upstream, on the enzyme that produces DHT.

answers.text: Finasteride inhibits 5-alpha-reductase, lowering DHT in tissues like the prostate and scalp that depend on DHT, while testosterone continues to act directly on muscle and brain

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. DHT binds the androgen receptor far more tightly than testosterone and dominates in the prostate, scalp, and skin. Testosterone itself acts directly on muscle and the hypothalamus without needing conversion, so blocking DHT formation spares those effects.

answers.text: Finasteride increases hepatic clearance of testosterone specifically in scalp and prostate tissue

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The liver does not selectively clear testosterone from particular peripheral tissues. Finasteride's action is enzymatic inhibition of 5-alpha-reductase at the tissue level, not altered hepatic metabolism.

answers.text: Finasteride competes with testosterone for GnRH receptors at the pituitary

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Finasteride has no action at the pituitary or on GnRH receptors. Its target is the peripheral enzyme 5-alpha-reductase, which converts testosterone to DHT.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the androgen receptor mechanism: DHT dominates in DHT-dependent tissues (prostate, scalp, skin), while testosterone itself drives effects in muscle and brain — this is exactly why blocking DHT formation is tissue-selective.
Well done — you've correctly linked the tissue-specific DHT dependence to finasteride's selective clinical effect.

interactions.label: A man with erectile dysfunction says he does not want to plan a PDE5 inhibitor d

params.question: A man with erectile dysfunction says he does not want to plan a PDE5 inhibitor dose around sexual activity and would prefer a medicine he can take once daily. Which drug best fits this preference, and why?

answers.text: Sildenafil, because food does not slow its absorption

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Food actually slows sildenafil's absorption, and it is taken on demand thirty to sixty minutes before sex — not suited to daily dosing.

answers.text: Tadalafil, because its long half-life allows once-daily dosing

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Tadalafil has a much longer half-life than the other PDE5 inhibitors, which is why it can be taken daily rather than on demand.

answers.text: Avanafil, because it acts within about fifteen minutes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Avanafil's advantage is rapid onset for on-demand use, not a long duration suited to daily dosing.

answers.text: Vardenafil, because it has the shortest duration of action among PDE5 inhibitors

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A short duration of action would make a drug less, not more, suitable for once-daily use; vardenafil is used on demand similarly to sildenafil.

overallFeedback.feedback: Recall the timing differences: sildenafil and vardenafil are on-demand, avanafil acts fastest, and tadalafil's long half-life is what makes daily dosing possible.
Right — tadalafil's long half-life is exactly what supports daily rather than on-demand dosing.

interactions.label: A breastfeeding woman is started on a progestogen-only ('mini') pill. Since this

params.question: A breastfeeding woman is started on a progestogen-only ('mini') pill. Since this method does not reliably suppress ovulation, which mechanism is primarily responsible for its contraceptive effect?

answers.text: Thickening of cervical mucus, preventing sperm from passing through

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Progesterone thickens and stickens cervical mucus, blocking sperm penetration — this is the main mechanism of progestin-only methods and still works even in cycles where ovulation isn't fully blocked.

answers.text: Complete suppression of FSH and LH at the hypothalamus and pituitary

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This is the primary mechanism of combined pills and DMPA, which reliably prevent ovulation. The question states ovulation is not reliably suppressed here, ruling this out.

answers.text: Copper ion-mediated impairment of sperm function

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes the copper IUD's mechanism, not a hormonal progestogen-only pill.

answers.text: Irreversible thinning of the endometrium preventing any future implantation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Endometrial thinning is a real but secondary, reversible backup mechanism — not the primary or permanent mechanism of the mini-pill.

overallFeedback.feedback: Re-examine the three targets: ovulation suppression (COC/DMPA), cervical mucus thickening (progestin-only pill's main action), and endometrial thinning (a backup mechanism).
Exactly — cervical mucus thickening is the dominant, reliable mechanism when ovulation itself isn't consistently blocked.

interactions.label: Why does inducing labour with oxytocin at 32 weeks of gestation often require mu

params.question: Why does inducing labour with oxytocin at 32 weeks of gestation often require much higher doses than induction at term?

answers.text: Myometrial oxytocin receptor density is far lower before term, rising up to 300-fold as term approaches

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. As term approaches, oxytocin receptor density on uterine muscle cells increases up to 300-fold, making the uterus far more sensitive to even small amounts of oxytocin. Before this rise, much higher doses are needed to produce the same effect.

answers.text: Progesterone levels are higher at 32 weeks than at term, increasing uterine sensitivity

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The opposite is true — progesterone dominates during pregnancy and keeps the uterus quiescent; it falls as term approaches, which is part of what allows the uterus to become sensitive to oxytocin.

answers.text: Gap junctions between myometrial cells are more developed at 32 weeks than at term

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Gap junctions form and allow synchronised contractions as term approaches, not before — the reverse of this statement.

answers.text: Placental nitric oxide production rises sharply at 32 weeks, relaxing the uterus further

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Nitric oxide-mediated relaxation is a feature of the quiescent state throughout pregnancy, but it is the fall in relaxing signals and rise in oxytocin receptors near term — not a 32-week nitric oxide surge — that explains the induction dose difference.

overallFeedback.feedback: Recall the at-term shift: progesterone falls, oxytocin receptors surge up to 300-fold, and gap junctions form — none of which have happened yet at 32 weeks, which is why induction needs much higher doses.
Right — the dramatic rise in oxytocin receptor density near term is what makes the uterus responsive to normal induction doses.

interactions.label: A woman presents with anovulatory infertility, hyperandrogenism, and insulin res

params.question: A woman presents with anovulatory infertility, hyperandrogenism, and insulin resistance consistent with polycystic ovary syndrome. Which drug combination is the most appropriate first-line management?

answers.text: Metformin plus an ovulation inducer such as letrozole or clomiphene

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. In PCOS, high androgens and insulin resistance prevent normal follicle development, so an insulin sensitiser like metformin is combined with an ovulation inducer like letrozole or clomiphene.

answers.text: Bromocriptine plus pulsatile GnRH

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This combination targets hyperprolactinaemia and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism respectively — different causes of anovulation, not PCOS.

answers.text: Exogenous gonadotropins alone

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Gonadotropins are reserved for hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, where FSH and LH are too low to stimulate the follicle — not the primary approach for PCOS, where the axis is intact.

answers.text: Progesterone supplementation alone

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Progesterone supports the uterine lining and is used for uterine factor infertility, not for restoring ovulation in PCOS.

overallFeedback.feedback: Match the cause to the drug: PCOS (insulin resistance + hyperandrogenism) needs metformin plus an ovulation inducer, hyperprolactinaemia needs a dopamine agonist, and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism needs gonadotropins or pulsatile GnRH.
Correct — metformin plus letrozole or clomiphene directly targets both the insulin resistance and the anovulation driving PCOS infertility.

interactions.label: A 68-year-old man on testosterone replacement therapy for confirmed hypogonadism

params.question: A 68-year-old man on testosterone replacement therapy for confirmed hypogonadism is newly diagnosed with untreated prostate cancer. What is the most appropriate next step regarding his testosterone therapy?

answers.text: Continue TRT unchanged, since testosterone does not influence prostate cancer growth

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Testosterone can drive growth of androgen-dependent prostate cancer, which is exactly why anti-androgen therapy is used to treat it. Continuing TRT unchanged is not appropriate.

answers.text: Halve the TRT dose and monitor PSA more closely

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Dose reduction does not remove the risk — active prostate cancer is an absolute contraindication to testosterone therapy, not a dose-adjustment situation.

answers.text: Stop TRT immediately, since active prostate cancer is an absolute contraindication to testosterone therapy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The video explicitly states testosterone therapy is completely contraindicated in active prostate cancer, since the tumour may depend on androgen signalling for growth.

answers.text: Switch from intramuscular testosterone to transdermal gel to lower prostate risk

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Changing the route of administration does not eliminate the androgen exposure driving a hormone-sensitive tumour — the contraindication applies regardless of delivery method.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the key integration point: TRT restores androgen function in hypogonadism, but active prostate cancer is a hard stop for testosterone therapy because the tumour may depend on androgen signalling.
Correct — active prostate cancer is an absolute contraindication to testosterone replacement therapy, regardless of dose or route.
